items.headline: Joao Pedro absence pushes Palmer sale into focus as Haaland remains Gameweek 11 captain
items.summary:
William Saliba is ready to return for Arsenal after building fitness in behind-closed-doors friendlies, making Ezri Konsa and Riccardo Calafiori less secure over a punishing run of Manchester City, Brentford, Spurs, Real Madrid and Bournemouth. Both are still expected to start at Newcastle in Gameweek 11, so an immediate sale is not essential, but neither is a buy. Gabriel remains the secure Arsenal defensive route, while Raya offers the set-and-forget goalkeeper option. Brighton defenders such as De Kuijper, Vuskovic and Van Hecke are attractive alternatives, particularly with Ipswich next.

Joao Pedro is ruled out of Chelsea's home match against Leeds and may not return until December, a blow both to his own ownership and to Cole Palmer's appeal. Chelsea have scored in only one league match without Joao Pedro this season, so Palmer's premium price looks increasingly difficult to justify even though he remains a start this week. Morgan Rogers is still a viable budget midfielder on form, but Joao Pedro is likely to be sold in Gameweek 12 rather than forced out now if there is no compelling forward replacement. Nicolas Jackson is the priority forward target behind Erling Haaland, with Alexander Isak a strong but expensive alternative and Evanilson, Barry and Dominic Calvert-Lewin cheaper routes.

Manchester United are a wait-and-see under Mauricio Pochettino, beginning with Liverpool away. Reports of a possible back-five shape from training only reinforce the uncertainty around roles, with Bruno Fernandes, Matheus Cunha and Joshua Zirkzee potentially benefiting more than wing-back options such as Brandon Williams. There is no case to buy a United player before Gameweek 11; assess their Liverpool, European and Brentford matches before targeting the improved fixtures from Gameweek 12 onwards.

Haaland is the clear captain at home to Fulham despite consecutive league blanks, with Jackson the leading vice-captain against Sunderland and Isak a credible differential at home to Manchester United. Wildcarding in Gameweek 11 is not advised because of uncertainty over United assets and the difficult choice between Bruno, Isak and Gabriel alongside Haaland. A bench boost is worth using now for managers already set up, while the current squad plan is to roll a transfer, start Joao Pedro only if necessary from the bench, and use two moves in Gameweek 12 to restructure around his absence and potentially move Palmer.
key_points: Saliba's return reduces Konsa and Calafiori's long-term security, although both are still expected to start at Newcastle in Gameweek 11.
Gabriel and Raya are Arsenal's safest defensive picks; De Kuijper, Vuskovic and Van Hecke are strong alternatives for Brighton's favourable fixtures.

Avoid a Gameweek 11 wildcard unless essential; use a well-prepared bench boost now rather than saving it without a clear future plan.

items.title: FPL GW11 Team Selection: Goodbye Konsa, Hello Free Hit! 💥 | Transfers & Captain
items.headline: Haaland is the clear Gameweek 11 captain as Konaté replacement becomes priority
items.summary:
Gameweek 11 is set up as a defence-heavy week, with Erling Haaland the standout captain at home to Fulham. Manchester City carry the highest projected goal total of the round and Haaland remains the focal point of their attack despite recent Premier League blanks. Nicolas Jackson, at home to Sunderland, is vice-captain, while Everton forward Barry keeps his place because he dominates Everton’s chance volume and arrives in strong finishing form.

The preferred starting defence is a four-man unit of Riccardo Calafiori, Ezri Konsa, Micky van de Ven and Thiago Silva, alongside Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya. Arsenal’s trip to Newcastle is considered better than it looks: Newcastle’s non-penalty xG has been among the weakest in the league, making Arsenal’s defensive triple-up appealing. Brighton have the best clean-sheet odds against Hull, strengthening the case for Van de Ven, while Silva remains a high-upside Bournemouth defender because of strong team defensive numbers, defensive-contribution potential and bonus appeal against Nottingham Forest.

The likely transfer is Konsa to Luka Vuskovic. William Saliba is nearing a return after friendly and Under-21 minutes, creating a growing risk that Konsa loses starts, minutes or defensive-contribution opportunities. Konsa may still start against Newcastle and could reach 60 minutes, but his long-term security is deteriorating. Vuskovic offers better immediate clean-sheet odds against Hull, stronger historical threat for defensive contributions and set-piece returns, and an appealing run in eight of the next nine gameweeks. The move also potentially catches a price rise.

Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers start against Leeds despite uninspiring recent underlying numbers, largely because midfield alternatives are unconvincing. Pascal Gross returns to the XI for Hull after being benched for 10 points in Gameweek 10; the earlier benching is accepted as an understandable differential call, but Gross’s next two fixtures are too good to ignore. Sharda is first substitute rather than a starter against Everton, with Callum Wilson now more likely than Sharda to take penalties if Thiago is unavailable. Bryan Mbeumo is retained despite Liverpool away, as his underlying data remains elite and Manchester United’s new-manager effect may help; Gameweek 16 at Arsenal is viewed as a more logical sale point.

Looking ahead, a Gameweek 13 Free Hit is planned to avoid Brighton versus Bournemouth and target players unavailable through normal transfers, notably Liverpool and Chelsea assets in a midweek round. Before that, the intended Gameweek 12 double move is Palmer and Barry out for Manzambi and Dominic Calvert-Lewin, subject to Manzambi’s fitness. That targets favourable fixtures before using the Free Hit to field a radically different side, potentially including double Liverpool defence, Chelsea attackers, Spurs defenders and Crystal Palace’s Daniel Muñoz.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Fulham in Gameweek 11, with Jackson at home to Sunderland as vice-captain.
Make Konsa to Vuskovic the priority transfer because Saliba’s return increasingly threatens Konsa’s minutes and upside.
Start Raya, Calafiori and Konsa against a low-output Newcastle attack, while Vuskovic is favoured for Brighton’s home match with Hull.

Plan Palmer and Barry to Manzambi and Calvert-Lewin in Gameweek 12, then deploy the Free Hit in Gameweek 13 to attack Liverpool, Chelsea, Spurs and Crystal Palace fixtures.

items.headline: Joao Pedro and Bukayo Saka headline Gameweek 11 injury absences
items.summary:
Fantasy Premier League managers face a busy Gameweek 11 team-news round, with Chelsea’s Joao Pedro the most important confirmed absentee. The forward has not returned to team training and is ruled out, while Bukayo Saka is expected to miss around another four weeks after Arsenal confirm he is only halfway through an eight-week rehabilitation period. Manchester City’s Erling Haaland has no reported fitness concern for Fulham, making him available for the early Saturday captaincy conversation despite the perceived risk of a 12:30pm kick-off.

Chelsea otherwise receive encouraging updates: Moises Caicedo is fit after illness concerns, Enzo Fernandez is available, and Aaron Anselmino is back in the squad, but Reece James, Max Lavia and Jamie Gittens remain unavailable or short of match fitness. Arsenal’s William Saliba has returned to action in youth and behind-closed-doors games, yet is still being managed carefully; Cristhian Mosquera is therefore likely to retain his place for now. Newcastle have few issues beyond Joelinton’s hamstring problem, while Liverpool expect Virgil van Dijk, Ryan Gravenberch, Jeremie Frimpong and Dominik Szoboszlai to be available.

There are several defensive and midfield concerns elsewhere. Aston Villa’s Matty Cash must follow concussion protocol after a head injury with Poland and is expected back in Gameweek 12, while Boubacar Kamara, Amadou Onana and Roger are still out. Sunderland lose Granit Xhaka to a potentially significant calf injury and Brian Brobbey to a thigh problem, although Omar Alderete returns from suspension. Nottingham Forest must assess Callum Hudson-Odoi, Nicolas Dominguez, Nicolas Williams and Alexander Schlager, while Brentford are particularly depleted: Nathan Collins and Aaron Hickey are sidelined for weeks and Igor Thiago begins a three-match suspension.

Managers considering attacking replacements should note that Bournemouth’s Justin Kluivert is ready to start and may increasingly threaten Eli Junior Kroupi’s role, while Alex Scott is being built up for starts over the next three matches. Tottenham have Lucas Bergvall, Destiny Udogie and James Maddison available again, but Mathys Tel is out for roughly three weeks. Everton welcome Jack Grealish back into the senior group and he is expected to be involved against Brentford. Fulham’s Josh King is fit despite recent groin pain, but Emile Smith Rowe misses out with a hip issue.
key_points: Erling Haaland has no reported fitness concern for Manchester City’s home match against Fulham and remains available for Gameweek 11 captaincy.
Joao Pedro is ruled out for Chelsea after failing to return to full training, making him a pressing transfer concern for his owners.
Bukayo Saka is expected to miss roughly another month, with Arsenal targeting a return around mid-December.
Brentford lose Nathan Collins and Aaron Hickey for weeks, while Igor Thiago starts a three-match ban after a failed appeal.
Matty Cash is unavailable for Aston Villa due to concussion protocol and is expected to return in Gameweek 12.
Granit Xhaka has a calf injury that is likely to keep him out for an extended spell, while Sunderland striker Brian Brobbey also misses Aston Villa with a thigh issue.

Liverpool expect Van Dijk, Gravenberch, Frimpong and Szoboszlai to be fit, with Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni back in partial training but not yet ready to play.

items.title: 🚨 João Pedro is OUT 🚨 FPL GW11 Final Thoughts 🤔
items.headline: Haaland is the locked captain as Konsa minutes become a growing concern in Gameweek 11
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the clear captain for Gameweek 11 at home to Fulham, while the main selection issue is whether to risk Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa at Newcastle. William Saliba is fit again after two behind-closed-doors matches and is expected to reclaim substantial minutes for Arsenal soon. Konsa may still start this week, but he is no longer secure enough to win close calls: Calafiori is preferred if choosing between the two Arsenal defenders, while reliable starters such as Iliman Ndiaye and Dominic Calvert-Lewin also rank ahead of Konsa in bench decisions.

João Pedro is ruled out for Chelsea in Gameweek 11 and has not returned to team training, making him a sell for most managers, particularly those without Nicolas Jackson. Jackson is viewed as a strong one-transfer replacement with a good five-week fixture run, while Hugo Ekitiké is also attractive if managers can afford him. Calvert-Lewin can be retained for now, with appealing home fixtures in Gameweeks 12 and 14. Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers remain starts against Leeds despite Chelsea looking less effective without João Pedro; his absence is a concern, but not sufficient reason alone to make a rushed sale before this fixture.

Among defenders, Jan Paul van Hecke offers the safest guaranteed minutes, Luka Vuskovic combines strong security with favourable medium-term fixtures, and Brighton’s Maxim De Cuyper has the highest upside if he keeps his place. De Cuyper is a viable buy despite the possible future threat from Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh, but buyers must accept that he may need selling again if his minutes decline. Konsa is the bigger longer-term sell than Calafiori because Saliba is expected to become Arsenal’s first-choice right-sided centre-back, whereas Calafiori remains first choice at left-back even if he is occasionally rested in congested periods.

Milos Kerkez is favoured over Bournemouth’s Marcos Senesi for new purchases despite Senesi’s superior defensive-contribution potential. Senesi is already on four yellow cards, creating a suspension risk that is manageable only for squads with strong cover. Kerkez has excellent Liverpool fixtures ahead, fewer disciplinary concerns and enough defensive-contribution potential to be a dependable alternative. The preferred personal Gameweek 11 setup is a 4-3-3, with Raya and Calafiori joining De Cuyper, Vuskovic and Van Hecke in defence; Palmer, Rogers and Pascal Gross in midfield; and Calvert-Lewin, Jackson and captain Haaland up front. Bryan Mbeumo is edged out by Calvert-Lewin, mainly because Calvert-Lewin is nailed for penalties and Chelsea’s defence has been vulnerable.

With three free transfers available, the recommendation is still to roll rather than force a marginal defensive move. A Gameweek 13 midweek round and the Christmas schedule should create more urgent injuries, rotation issues and opportunities, making transfer flexibility especially valuable. Managers considering a Bench Boost can likely use it with Bobby Thomas if he returns to Coventry’s starting side after training, but should delay or use a transfer if they are unconvinced he starts.
key_points: Captain Haaland at home to Fulham in Gameweek 11; the armband is described as locked.
Sell João Pedro in most squads after confirmation that he is out for Gameweek 11 and not yet training with Chelsea.
Start Palmer and Rogers against Leeds, but reassess Palmer before Gameweek 12 if João Pedro’s absence continues to hurt Chelsea’s attack.
Bench Konsa in close calls despite a likely start at Newcastle, as Saliba’s return creates a significant medium-term minutes risk.
Van Hecke is the safest defensive purchase, Vuskovic is the secure longer-term option, and De Cuyper has the greatest upside if his starts continue.
Prefer Kerkez to buying Senesi for Liverpool’s fixture run because Senesi is one yellow card from suspension.
Calvert-Lewin is preferred to Mbeumo for the final attacking spot, with penalties and Chelsea’s defensive weakness breaking a close call.
Avoid forcing a transfer and preserve flexibility for the Gameweek 13 midweek round and Christmas congestion.

items.headline: Van Hecke and Vuskovic top the Gameweek 11 defensive shopping list
items.summary:
Gameweek 11 is framed as a week to prioritise reliable minutes, particularly after the international break and before the fixture schedule becomes more congested. Brighton’s Jan Paul van Hecke and Tottenham’s Luka Vuskovic stand out as the preferred defensive additions: both combine strong fixtures, clean-sheet potential, defensive-contribution points and attacking threat. Van Hecke hosts Hull, while Vuskovic faces Ipswich at home; Vuskovic is viewed as the premium long-term option, but Van Hecke is an equally attractive immediate transfer for managers without a Brighton defender.

Lewis Hall is a recommended sale for either Van Hecke or Vuskovic, with the choice depending on squad structure. Managers who already own Djed Spence/Dalot-type budget defensive cover should take Van Hecke first and plan for Vuskovic later; ideally, both are acquired soon. Arsenal’s Cristhian Mosquera is also backed to start against Newcastle despite William Saliba nearing fitness, but there is acknowledgement that Saliba’s return creates a looming selection risk. Selling Mosquera for Van Hecke is nevertheless supported, especially with Tottenham hosting Ipswich and Brighton hosting Hull.

Captaincy is a close call between Erling Haaland at home to Fulham, Alexander Isak at home to Manchester United and Nicolas Jackson. Haaland is not a recommended sale before Fulham, even for a route to Jackson and Bruno Fernandes, as the immediate fixture is too good to ignore. Isak is an appealing differential captain because Manchester United’s new-manager bounce is not expected to transform a fragile defence instantly, although Haaland remains the safer default. Jackson is also endorsed as an excellent forward option, but not at the cost of selling Haaland this week.

Bench decisions favour security of starts over speculative upside. Barry is preferred to Manzambi, whose minutes and fitness are less dependable, while Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall should start ahead of Manzambi. Morgan Gibbs-White is the suggested bench option when compared with Liverpool’s Florian Wirtz and Cole Palmer, while Mohamed Mahmoevic is the preferred bench over Palmer or Rodoni. For midfield transfers, John McGinn is preferred to a speculative Aston Villa teammate, though Rodoni is a sensible cheaper option for a one-week Bench Boost or for managers wanting money reserved for Bruno Fernandes later.

A Bench Boost is only considered worthwhile if Bobby Thomas is fit enough to start for Coventry. The proposed bench of Kinsky against Ipswich, Silva, Thomas and Josh King is viewed as playable, but Thomas returning to training without a firm start guarantee makes the chip too risky. João Pedro is also treated as a major doubt after posting that his recovery is being taken ‘day by day’, so managers should not assume he starts.
key_points: Buy Jan Paul van Hecke or Luka Vuskovic if possible, with both regarded as elite defensive picks for Gameweek 11 and the following weeks.
Sell Lewis Hall for Van Hecke or Vuskovic; Van Hecke is the immediate preference for managers who need Brighton coverage against Hull.
Do not sell Erling Haaland before Manchester City host Fulham, even if the move funds Nicolas Jackson and Bruno Fernandes.
Alexander Isak is a viable captain against Manchester United, as a new manager is unlikely to fix their defensive problems immediately.
Prioritise players with secure 90-minute potential after the international break: start Barry over Manzambi and Dewsbury-Hall over Manzambi.
Bench Boost only if Bobby Thomas is confirmed fit to start; otherwise hold the transfer and delay the chip.
Treat João Pedro as doubtful rather than assuming he plays, given the lack of a clear recovery timetable.
Florian Wirtz is preferred to Mohammed Kudus as a Liverpool midfield buy, with strong underlying numbers and favourable fixtures.

The recommended Gameweek 11 squad is built around Erling Haaland as the non-negotiable premium, with the Manchester City forward started every week and captained in most rounds. Nicolas Jackson partners him in a two-man forward line, backed by strong Aston Villa fixtures and prolific recent form. The structure deliberately spends heavily on Haaland, Arsenal’s defence and Bruno Fernandes while finding value in lower-priced midfield and defensive options.

David Raya is the preferred goalkeeper as the first-choice keeper behind the league’s best defence, and Gabriel completes an Arsenal double-up. Gabriel is viewed as Arsenal’s most reliable long-term defensive starter despite his higher price. The team uses a four-man defence, with Vuskovic, Vaneka and Antonio Silva selected alongside Gabriel because they offer defensive-contribution potential as well as enough attacking threat to produce major hauls.

Bruno Fernandes is the premium midfield choice, although the slot can go to another premium depending on preference. Fernandes is backed as a possible beneficiary of a new-manager bounce and has upcoming captaincy potential. The rest of midfield is intentionally inexpensive: Ajer is picked for the immediate Nottingham Forest fixture, Gross is retained as one of the few midfielders showing consistent appeal, and Manzambi is a target if available because Aston Villa’s forthcoming schedule is especially favourable. The cheap midfield approach reflects a market in which few midfielders are producing enough to justify major investment.

The bench is designed for rotation rather than simply filling the squad cheaply. Barry can cover tougher fixtures for starting players, while Mhmic is the fifth defender and becomes particularly useful in Gameweeks 12 and 14, when his fixture run is strongest. Dal, priced at £4.3m, fills the final midfield slot. The main trade-off is accepting a thin, low-cost midfield in order to fund Haaland, Jackson, a strong Arsenal defensive double-up and a premium midfielder; it relies on defenders and forwards continuing to provide the most reliable returns.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin is retained for Coventry at home in Gameweek 12, while KZA's sale can wait until Gameweek 12 or 13.
Sangari is a third-bench player and not an immediate transfer priority.

items.title: SELL PALMER (& ROGERS?) FPL GW11! 😮 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 Chelsea Failing… #fpl #premierleague #chelsea
items.headline: Cole Palmer faces FPL sale pressure as Chelsea await João Pedro return
items.summary:
Cole Palmer is the Chelsea midfielder most at risk of an FPL exit, particularly if João Pedro remains unavailable after the international break. Chelsea score in only one of the four matches João Pedro has missed this season, underlining how much the Brazilian striker’s presence can improve the attack and the prospects of players around him. If he returns, Palmer and Morgan Rogers become easier holds; if not, Palmer’s premium price looks increasingly difficult to justify.

Palmer’s concern is not solely Chelsea’s dependence on João Pedro. His recent displays lack the usual quality in link-up play and finishing, while his FPL output trails Rogers despite costing around £2m more. The eye test also favours Rogers, making it hard to argue that the Aston Villa midfielder is the bigger problem in a squad containing Palmer.

Rogers remains a comfortable long-term hold, potentially for the next 20 gameweeks, because of his price, the value already tied up in him and his stronger relative output. Palmer is the player to sell if a midfield transfer is required, although the lack of compelling midfield replacements limits the urgency to move either player. The principal risk of selling Palmer is Chelsea winning penalties, which can quickly restore his appeal.
key_points: Chelsea score in only one of four matches without João Pedro, so his post-international-break availability is crucial for Palmer’s FPL outlook.
Cole Palmer is the preferred Chelsea midfielder to sell if a transfer is needed, despite the risk of losing his penalty potential.
Morgan Rogers is a long-term hold because of his lower price, retained team value and better recent output relative to Palmer.
Palmer’s recent performances raise concerns beyond João Pedro’s absence, with his finishing and general quality on the ball below expectations.
There is no urgent need to sell either midfielder while attractive replacement options in midfield remain limited.

items.title: HAALAND & ISAK 🚀 | AZ's FPL GW 11 Team Selection
items.headline: Haaland gets the armband at Fulham as three free transfers loom
items.summary:
The November-December schedule is treated as a season-defining period, making squad depth and flexibility especially valuable. The current wildcard-built squad is in good shape, with Kinsky and Trafford forming a reliable goalkeeper pairing. Kinsky is set to return for Tottenham's home fixture against Ipswich, while Van Hecke also benefits from a favourable home match.

The defence of Van Hecke, Silva, Vuskovic and Gabriel is viewed as close to the strongest available setup. In midfield, Rogers and Gross are straightforward selections, but the key decision is between Man Zambi and Tavernier. Man Zambi has the more appealing fixture against Sunderland rather than Tavernier's match with Nottingham Forest, although an injury doubt and less secure minutes make the choice one to monitor close to the deadline.

Erling Haaland is captain for Manchester City's trip to Fulham. Isak is backed against Manchester United, with Pochettino expected to need time to settle his new side; Liverpool are therefore strongly favoured to win that fixture. Jackson completes the forward line.

No transfer is planned over the international break unless new injury news emerges. Holding the move would take the squad to three free transfers, offering valuable room to react during the congested festive run and reinforcing the view that the wildcard has delivered the desired balance and cover.
key_points: Captain Haaland for Manchester City's away fixture at Fulham.
Start Kinsky at home to Ipswich, with Trafford retained as the second goalkeeper.
Van Hecke is a favoured defensive pick because of his home fixture, alongside Silva, Vuskovic and Gabriel.
Man Zambi is narrowly preferred to Tavernier because Sunderland is a better fixture than Nottingham Forest, but his injury status and minutes are concerns.
Back Isak against Pochettino's Manchester United, with Liverpool expected to win the match.
Roll the transfer unless injuries intervene, which creates three free transfers for the festive schedule.

items.title: MY FPL GW11 TEAM SELECTION! 🔥 SPEND TWO TRANSFERS 🤔
items.headline: Haaland retains the armband as Jackson move tops Gameweek 11 transfer plans
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the preferred captain for Gameweek 11 despite a blank against Nottingham Forest before the international break, with Cole Palmer the vice-captain. The front line is led by Evanilson Barry, who is delivering exceptional value at £5.7m and sits just six points behind Alexander Isak despite Isak’s seven goals in nine matches. João Pedro completes the attack but is a major selection concern ahead of Leeds, with a pre-deadline fitness update likely to decide whether he starts, is benched or is sold.

The defence currently starts Raya away to Newcastle, De Cuyper against Hull, Van Hecke against Ipswich and Arsenal’s Mosquera/Concer. However, Raya’s £6.2m price is increasingly difficult to justify when cheaper goalkeepers such as Verbruggen and Trafford are close on points. Brighton have the best clean-sheet odds for Gameweek 11 at 40%, ahead of Manchester City and Arsenal on 38%, while De Cuyper remains an outstanding budget asset despite likely rotation at some point. Arsenal’s selection is complicated by Saliba’s return to training and match fitness, which could eventually threaten Concer’s place.

The key midfield bench call is Bryan Mbeumo versus Sharda, with Sharda currently preferred because of the home fixture and the possibility of playing centrally while Thiago serves a three-match ban. Mbeumo has not returned since arriving in the squad, although a managerial change at Manchester United could improve his prospects. Chelsea’s attack also warrants caution: it has produced only 7.5 xG over the last six matches, the league’s sixth-worst total, albeit João Pedro has missed half of those games. Gross and Silva are both one booking from suspension, leaving the squad vulnerable if either is banned.

With two free transfers and £1.3m in the bank, João Pedro to Jackson is the leading move, particularly with Jackson offering a strong Gameweek 12 captaincy route away to Ipswich after Sunderland at home. Concer to Vaskovic is also appealing because Vaskovic combines goal threat, defensive-contribution potential and a solid defence at a low price, but it may be postponed: Arsenal’s clean-sheet odds are comparable to Brighton’s this week, and retaining a transfer preserves flexibility. The preferred plan is Jackson in and one transfer saved unless Concer looks unlikely to start, in which case both moves become viable.

Looking further ahead, Gameweek 12 could be a roll, although Haaland away at Arsenal may become a rare benching debate. Gameweek 14 is pencilled in as a potential Free Hit because Chelsea v Liverpool and the North London derby make several existing assets less attractive, while Bournemouth host Hull, Leeds host Ipswich and Manchester United host Coventry. The longer-term aim is to restore double Arsenal defence, potentially bring João Pedro back after Aston Villa’s favourable run ends, and consider selling Mbeumo before Arsenal in Gameweek 16 to fund Gabriel.
key_points: Captain Haaland in Gameweek 11, with Palmer as vice-captain; Barry is a tempting alternative after his 16-point haul and sustained value output.
João Pedro to Jackson is the priority transfer, subject to the latest João Pedro fitness news before the Leeds deadline.
Concer to Vaskovic is under consideration but can wait until Gameweek 12 unless Saliba’s return makes Concer’s start doubtful.
Start Sharda over Mbeumo, largely due to the home fixture and a possible striker role during Thiago’s three-match suspension.
Gross and Silva are each one yellow card away from a suspension, making squad depth and transfer flexibility especially important.
Raya is becoming difficult to justify at £6.2m, with Verbruggen and Trafford offering similar points totals for significantly less.
Gameweek 12 presents a potential Haaland benching decision away to Arsenal, while Jackson could become a captaincy candidate against Ipswich.
Gameweek 14 is a leading Free Hit target due to difficult fixtures for Chelsea, Liverpool, Arsenal and Brighton assets alongside attractive one-week alternatives.

items.title: Transfer 🔒 more this week or next? 🤔 My FPL Team for GW11 🔥
items.headline: Haaland is the clear Gameweek 11 captain as Andy resists further transfers
items.summary:
Andy enters Gameweek 11 at 110,000 overall after a 59-point red arrow in Gameweek 10, despite returns from his Arsenal defence, Pascal Groß and Nicolas Jackson. His early move during the international break is Lewis Hall to Vuskovic, leaving him with three free transfers and £1.8m in the bank. He accepts the risk of acting early because Vuskovic was a planned purchase and rising in price, while Hall was the clear player to sell.

The move gives him a Brighton defensive double-up of Vuskovic and De Cuyper, with Vuskovic valued for set-piece threat and defensive-contribution points, and De Cuyper for his advanced open-play role. He also starts Raya and Calafiori against Newcastle, judging the visitors' attack sufficiently blunt to justify backing Arsenal's defence. Konsa is currently first substitute, although he remains in contention to start over Calafiori; Andy favours Calafiori's greater attacking potential if forced to choose.

In midfield, Mbeumo is selected despite Liverpool away, alongside Palmer and Rogers at home to Leeds and Groß away to Hull. There is some temptation to bench Mbeumo for Konsa or Calvert-Lewin, but Andy expects Mbeumo to retain regular minutes and likes his fixtures from Gameweeks 12 to 15. He sees no need to use a transfer on third-bench midfielder Sangare merely to create another difficult selection decision. Palmer remains despite poor value and underwhelming underlying numbers: he has penalties, a good Gameweek 11 fixture and is not worth selling for a cheaper midfielder unless funds are specifically required.

Up front, Jackson hosts Sunderland, Haaland hosts Fulham and Calvert-Lewin is benched for Chelsea away. Haaland is the captain over the in-form Jackson because his open-play goal threat is far higher and he has penalty duties. Andy is also content to delay any João Pedro move even if he is declared fit, given his recent injuries and uncertain minutes. Looking ahead, the main strategic decision is whether to buy Bruno Fernandes for Gameweeks 12 to 15, potentially funded by selling Palmer and Calafiori, or preserve transfers and use the Free Hit in Gameweek 14. He currently leans towards the Gameweek 14 Free Hit, which can target Bournemouth's home match against Hull and avoids committing several transfers to a short-term Fernandes move before returning to Palmer and eventually upgrading Jackson to João Pedro.
key_points: Haaland is captain for Gameweek 11 at home to Fulham, ahead of Nicolas Jackson against Sunderland.
Lewis Hall is sold early for Vuskovic, creating a Brighton defensive double-up with De Cuyper.
No further Gameweek 11 transfer is planned; three free transfers and £1.8m are retained for flexibility.
Calafiori is preferred to Konsa if only one starts, although Konsa is a strong first substitute and could still enter a back five.
Mbeumo is currently selected at Liverpool, but Konsa and Calvert-Lewin remain alternatives for the final starting place.
Palmer stays for Leeds at home despite poor value, with a future Palmer-to-Bruno Fernandes move under consideration for Gameweek 12.
João Pedro is not an immediate buy because of fitness and minutes concerns; Gameweek 13 or 16 are more likely entry points.
A Gameweek 14 Free Hit is currently favoured over buying Bruno Fernandes early, with Bournemouth's Hull home fixture a key target.

items.title: FPL GW11 BEST PLAYERS TO BUY! 🔴🇵🇹 CONSIDERING BRUNO F? #fpl  #premierleague
items.headline: Van Hecke leads Gameweek 11 defensive buys as Jackson tops the forward shortlist
items.summary:
Van Hecke is the leading defender target for Gameweek 11 because of his immediate fixtures, Double Gameweek appeal and attacking potential. Spurs are viewed as particularly strong defensively for their double, making Van Hecke the preferred short-term purchase. Vuskovic is another attractive option and is rated safer than Kai Penal, with a heavy upcoming schedule and the prospective returns of Minter and Matoma strengthening the case. Bournemouth's Antonio Silva completes the defensive shortlist thanks to strong long-term fixtures and Double Gameweek potential.

Midfield transfers are less straightforward, but Manzambi is a viable route into Aston Villa's attack for managers who already own Jackson and want to double up. Tavernier is a cheaper Bournemouth attacking option, especially for those unable to afford Evan Nelson, with Bournemouth's fixture run remaining favourable. However, Tavernier is on four yellow cards and carries a suspension risk. Pascal Gross is the standout midfield recommendation for non-owners: he is also one booking from a ban, but his form for Brighton and reliable minutes make him difficult to ignore.

Up front, Jackson is the preferred Gameweek 11 buy, with Sunderland at home and Aston Villa's upcoming fixtures driving the recommendation. Evan Nelson is next after scoring five goals in five matches, while Barry offers a budget alternative with appealing longer-term fixtures despite managers having missed his Gameweek 10 haul against Coventry. For a cheap goalkeeper, Spurs are the preferred source; Kinski is recommended for managers who cannot afford David Wright, given Spurs' defensive outlook and favourable short-term schedule.
key_points: Buy Van Hecke for the best short-term defensive fixture run, Double Gameweek potential and attacking threat.
Vuskovic is preferred to Kai Penal as a safer defensive pick with a busy schedule ahead and Minter and Matoma nearing returns.
Antonio Silva is a Bournemouth defensive option for managers targeting strong long-term fixtures and Double Gameweek upside.
Jackson is the top forward target for Gameweek 11, with Sunderland at home and Aston Villa's fixture run supporting the move.
Evan Nelson has scored five in five and remains a strong Bournemouth forward option, while Barry provides a cheaper long-term route.
Pascal Gross is a priority midfield buy for non-owners because of his Brighton form and secure minutes, but he is on four yellow cards.
Tavernier is also on four yellow cards, so his suspension risk must be considered before buying.
Kinski is the suggested budget goalkeeper if David Wright is unaffordable, with Spurs expected to offer short-term defensive value.
